items.topic: SSE vs WebSocket for real-time push
items.context: The spec calls for SSE, but the ecosystem-manager (our only existing real-time reference) uses WebSocket with Gorilla. SSE is simpler for unidirectional push (native EventSource API, auto-reconnect, no library needed), but WebSocket is proven in our codebase and could be reused if other endpoints need bidirectional communication later.

options.label: SSE with standard net/http
options.rationale: Unidirectional push is all we need. Native browser EventSource API handles reconnection automatically. No external dependency (Gorilla). Simpler implementation (~150 lines for broker). Recommended because the operations lens is strictly server→client push with no client→server messages needed.

options.label: WebSocket reusing ecosystem-manager patterns
options.rationale: Proven in our codebase. Could handle future bidirectional needs (e.g., client requesting specific node subscriptions). But adds Gorilla dependency and complexity we don't need for pure push.

items.context: The captures handler manages captures via direct filesystem access (reading captures/{id}/capture.json). The graph projection needs to list all captures with their classifications. Currently there's no CaptureLister interface — the handler does everything inline. We need to decide how to expose capture data to the graph package without creating a circular dependency.

options.label: Extract CaptureLister interface in graph package, implement in captures handler
options.rationale: Define a minimal interface in internal/graph/interfaces.go (e.g., ListCaptures() returning capture structs). The captures handler (or a thin adapter) implements it. Follows the existing adapter pattern (like BacklogLister wrapping backlog.Store). Recommended because it's consistent with how overview service consumes backlog data.

options.label: Add ListAll() method to captures package, expose as a standalone service
options.rationale: Refactor captures into a proper service layer (separate from handler). Cleaner long-term but more invasive — captures is currently handler-only with no service abstraction.

options.label: Read captures filesystem directly from graph package
options.rationale: Graph package reads captures/{id}/capture.json directly. Avoids cross-package dependency. But duplicates filesystem logic and couples graph to capture storage format.

items.topic: EventDispatcher injection points in execution service
items.context: The execution service manages state transitions through several methods (startLocked, Cancel, handleSpecSyncComplete, spawnFixupRun, TriggerReview, etc.). The callback EventDispatcher needs to be called at the right points. Adding a new dependency to the Service constructor changes its signature, which affects all test setup code.

options.label: Optional EventDispatcher field with setter method
options.rationale: Add a SetEventDispatcher(d EventDispatcher) method to execution.Service. If nil, dispatch calls are no-ops. Doesn't change the constructor signature, so existing tests are unaffected. Wire it in main.go after construction. Recommended because it's minimally invasive and follows the SetSettingsReader pattern already used in agentmanager.

options.label: Add EventDispatcher to Service constructor
options.rationale: Explicit dependency — can't forget to wire it. But requires updating every test that creates a Service, and the constructor already has 6+ parameters. Makes the dependency graph more rigid.

items.context: Captures have classification.Items with kind+title+description. BacklogItems have kind+name+title. The classified_as edge should connect a Capture to the BacklogItem(s) it was classified into. But classification items are suggestions — they may not have been accepted yet (no backlog item created). Need to decide what constitutes a match.

options.label: Match on exact kind+title against existing backlog items
options.rationale: For each classification item, look for a backlog item with matching kind and title. Only emit classified_as edge if a match exists. Simple and correct — if the user accepted the classification, the backlog item exists with that title. Recommended because it's deterministic and avoids false edges.

options.label: Always emit edges from capture to classification suggestions (even unaccepted)
options.rationale: Shows the full classification picture including pending suggestions. But creates edges to non-existent nodes, which breaks the graph contract.

options.label: Track accepted classifications explicitly via a field on the capture
options.rationale: Add an 'accepted_items' field to capture.json linking to actual backlog item keys. Most accurate but requires schema changes to the capture model.

items.text: The ecosystem-manager uses WebSocket (Gorilla) with a fan-out broadcaster goroutine, not SSE. Its pattern — broadcast channel, non-blocking sends, client map with RWMutex — is directly adaptable to an SSE broker by replacing websocket.Conn with http.ResponseWriter+Flusher. The core broadcast logic is the same regardless of transport.

plan_updates: Significantly expanded plan based on round 1 resolutions and deep codebase exploration. Key additions: (1) Added data-source table mapping each node type to its concrete Go access pattern, (2) Added interfaces.go file in Phase 1 defining all 6 data-source interfaces, (3) Detailed SSE connection lifecycle with heartbeat and full-sync on connect, (4) Specified EventDispatcher injection strategy following existing SetSettingsReader pattern, (5) Added Run node derivation strategy — no listing API, derive from ExecutionRecord.RunID with bounded errgroup, (6) Added agent-manager graceful degradation details, (7) Added ecosystem-manager WebSocket reference to Required Reading, (8) Expanded risks with capture listing and concurrent RunState lookup mitigations.
